_comment: setup-pipeline.ps1 CREATES this role itself (as AKSManagerCertManager) when it
does not exist, and assigns it to the certificate job's identity on each
PUBLIC zone in hosted-zones.json. This file is the same definition, for
reference or for creating it yourself:
az role definition create --role-definition @example-cert-manager-role.json
after replacing SUBSCRIPTION_ID in AssignableScopes with every subscription
that holds one of your public zones, and deleting this _comment key (az
rejects unknown keys). An existing definition's permissions are never
changed by setup, so a narrower one of your own is kept.
To use a different role instead (e.g. the built-in DNS Zone Contributor,
which allows every record type in the zone), set CERT_DNS_ROLE before
running setup; nothing is then created.
Assigned at ZONE scope, never record-set scope: lego deletes the
_acme-challenge record after validating, which would delete a record-set
assignment with it.
This is the tightest role in the system: TXT records in one zone, and
nothing else. It cannot create or change A or CNAME records, so it could not
be used to repoint a hostname. It is one step wider than the AWS equivalent,
which is also limited to names beginning _acme-challenge -- Azure RBAC has no
condition on DNS record names.
Name: AKSManagerCertManager
Description: Write TXT records in a public DNS zone for Let's Encrypt DNS-01 validation. Nothing else.
